account:
Today’s most unusual business is a large order for 200 loaves. The secretary says freight called it his order and personally gave the baker 24 emeralds and 72 wheat. Another 528 wheat is reportedly needed, with hauling to be arranged tomorrow. The mill’s hay price is reported as two emeralds per bale, yielding nine wheat, but stock and delivery terms remain unconfirmed. I do not know the order’s purpose, final recipient, or firm deadline. It may be an ordinary private bulk purchase; there is no evidence yet of a town commitment, and I have authorized no treasury payment. The treasury held 128 emeralds, but no ledger or supporting accounts were available today.

The builder requested a great hall lighting inspection tomorrow at 18:00, explaining that the new lanterns need checking for even illumination. That is a stated practical purpose, not evidence of some other gathering. My mill inspection is tomorrow at 10:00. The secretary has recorded the lighting appointment and gathered supply enquiries; the book just handed to me is titled Appointment Addendum, and I have not yet read it.

At tea, the neighbour reported peaceful docks and said the baker explained the lights as an oven baking fresh bread. The neighbour mentioned vague bridge and port rumours but could provide nothing concrete. I heard distant calls from the baker, innkeeper and builder without making out their words, so cannot infer their meaning. I feel there may be activity I do not understand, particularly around the bread order and tomorrow’s hauling, but I have no sound basis to claim a secret purpose or connect it to the hall lighting inspection. Direct questions to freight, the baker and miller are the appropriate next way to establish facts.
